name: Elvis Presley
hook: The singer whose first single, a blues song played at twice the speed, made Sun Records and then RCA the centre of rock and roll.
blurb: Elvis Presley was born in Tupelo, Mississippi, in 1935 and grew up in Memphis. On 5 July 1954, at Sun Studio, he and two musicians, Scotty Moore on electric guitar and Bill Black on string bass, started fooling around with an old blues song, 'That's All Right' by Arthur Crudup, and played it much faster. Sam Phillips recorded it, and it came out as Sun 209 on 19 July with the bluegrass song 'Blue Moon of Kentucky' on the other side: a Black songwriter's blues and a white country song on one record. A Memphis radio DJ played it over and over that month. Crudup, who wrote it and recorded it for RCA in 1946, stopped recording in the 1950s over unpaid royalties. A 1968 agreement to pay him $60,000 fell through when the publisher, Hill and Range, would not sign, and by 1971 he had collected a little over $10,000 (Wikipedia's article on Crudup). He died in 1974. RCA bought Presley's contract in 1955, and 'Heartbreak Hotel' (1956) was his first national number one. Within two years he was the most famous singer in the world. He died in 1977.
